frameworks.name: Oxygen Mask Priority Framework
frameworks.definition: Solve immediate survival constraints (ability to pay rent) before attempting long-term vision planning; basic needs security enables strategic thinking.

claims.text: Goals worth pursuing have clear action steps; everything else is distraction (Hormozi). Do not follow vague shoulds—instead, choose specific outcomes (getting in shape, getting married, making money) where the path is observable and actionable.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Clear action steps filter out distraction; vague shoulds provide no navigation.
bounded_by: Does not apply to exploratory or discovery-phase goals without observable endpoints

claims.text: Founders cannot think strategically about long-term vision (10-year horizon) until basic income security is established (ability to pay rent). The immediate cash-constraint problem blocks abstract planning.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: founder in pre-revenue or subsistence-income stage
claims.mechanism: Maslow-like hierarchy: survival anxiety fills cognitive bandwidth, preventing long-term strategic thinking.

claims.text: The non-work hours (5 PM - 9 AM) total eight hours daily plus two full days per week; founders have more discretionary hours than work hours. A job is not the constraint preventing goal pursuit unless the founder already possesses desired resources.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: founder does not yet have resource target
claims.mechanism: Time scarcity is a narrative excuse; actual available hours are abundant relative to single-threaded work.

anchors.region: non-work hours per day (5 PM - 9 AM + 2 weekend days)
work hours per day (9 AM - 5 PM)

bounded_by: Does not apply to founders with dependents or caregiving obligations
Does not apply to jobs with travel/on-call requirements

claims.text: Gym Launch's mission was operationalized as 'not be broke' rather than an aspirational vision. Achieving cash-positive status was the filtering condition that enabled subsequent wealth-building decisions.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: early-stage service business in commodity market
claims.mechanism: Survival goal provides unambiguous direction when more ambitious goals would invite debate and misalignment.
bounded_by: Does not apply to mission-driven or purpose-first businesses

claims.text: Whether a founder personally cares about wealth-as-status is irrelevant to whether they pursue wealth-as-solution. The initial goal is income security (not being broke) rather than personal enrichment aspiration.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Motivation source (shame, pain, purpose, curiosity) is independent from outcome; wealth-building works the same regardless of emotional origin.

examples.text: Alex Hormozi started Gym Launch with a mission statement of 'not be broke' rather than a visionary ten-year goal. The company achieved cash-positive status first, which then enabled subsequent wealth-building and scaling decisions. The low-bar mission created clarity on what mattered (revenue) versus what was distraction (vision, brand, expansion).

practices.text: When starting a business, default to survival-first goals (cash positive, able to pay rent) before attempting strategic vision work. This is not a ceiling but a gate—it forces clarity.
Do not wait for perfect alignment or aspirational mission clarity. Choose a specific, operational goal with clear action steps (get in shape, get married, make money) and execute it ruthlessly.
